newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end up after Greenspan's testimony.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end up after Greenspan's testimony.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher, as Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress reinforced beliefs that the U.S. central bank would not raise rates at the next policy meeting, traders said.
"We dodged a big bullet today," one Eurodollar futures trader said after midday.

March T-bonds and Eurodollar contracts fell to session lows in an immediate reaction to Greenspan's testimony, but bounced on a second reading of his comments and on technical factors. Traders were impressed with March T-bonds' ability to hold above last week's low of 110-05/32.
Greenspan's comments that a period of subdued wage growth may be coming to an end, and that the economy has retained "considerable vigor," instantly ignited selling.

However, his acknowledgment that price inflation remained under control led several commission houses to buy March slightly above the day's low at the 110-08/32 to 110-10/32 area. About this time, one Japanese firm bought 2,000 to 3,000 10-year notes.
"We bounced quicker than you can imagine," said one Eurodollar futures trader, who noted similar pockets of buying in June, September and December Eurodollar contracts.
The heavy commission house buying sparked heavy short-covering from the pit.
"The fact Greenspan didn't say much about stocks is alone a good enough reason for the market to bounce up here," one bond futures floor source said.

"Clearly, Greenspan is being cautious," another bond trader said. "He went from 'irrational exuberance' to 'breathtaking,'" he said. "It sounds like he is looking at a piece of art instead of the stock market."

In the question-and-answer period after his testimony, Greenspan said his "irrational exuberance" comment on the U.S. stock market was an attempt to explain how developments in asset markets figure into monetary policy decisions.
Several market analysts, however, were perplexed with Greenspan's statement that a higher U.S. savings rate was "crucial," in view of massive inflows into mutual funds.
"Is he trying to tell us that the gains in the S&Ps won't last forever?" one trader said.
Regardless, March bonds and Eurodollars continued to grind higher, with September Euros testing resistance at 94.05.
Traders said June Eurodollars would probably hit resistance at 94.24 in the near term. Above that level, traders are looking at 94.31 as major resistance.
March T-bonds edged closer to key resistance at 111-22/32 to 111-23/32 after one East Coast fund bought between 2,000 to 3,000 contracts in the final minutes of pit trade.
"The pit is still short," one trader said, adding that one prominent local trader was extremely short.
"He doesn't care what he is paying," he said.
At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were up 18/32 at 111-16/32, and June Euros were up two bps at 94.21.
